differences.message_quote: WBS (Raman 2026) extracts its direction from bench's `directed_modulation` items that *name the concept* (clavicle, bishop…) in both think/don't-think prompts.

message_source_quote: WBS (Raman 2026) extracts its direction from bench's `directed_modulation` items that *name the concept* (clavicle, bishop…) in both think/don't-think prompts. SMSS names no concept — the stance is over the carrier's own situation.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026, *white-bear steering*) showed that a *stance* direction — "think about X while writing" vs "don't think about X", with the concept X named in both prompts — lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on this exact model/lens, by pushing the model into a "hold-something-in-mind while doing something else" mode that the downstream layers carry into the read cell.
rationale: Both documents name Raman 2026 / white-bear steering (WBS) explicitly, describe SMSS as building on and distinguishing itself from it (concept-free vs. concept-named contrast, cosine 0.57–0.63, projection/residual tests), and make the same core novelty claim that the gain is not a recycled WBS signal. The write-up additionally gives WBS's own quantitative result (0.14→0.83) and cites a specific prior WBS ablation (§5.7 'hold vs mention') that failed, supporting its novelty argument in more detail than the closing message, which states the same conclusion more briefly without these supporting facts.
